seoTitle: How to Create an Asana Task From Email Easily
metaDescription: Find out how to forward emails into Asana in 2026 using your project's unique email address, so subject lines and bodies map straight into new tasks.
intro: Every Asana project has a hidden email address that turns forwarded messages into tasks, which is a fast way to capture action items without opening a browser. This guide explains how to find that address, format your email correctly, and use CC or syntax to set assignees and due dates right from your inbox.

steps.heading: Find your project's email address
steps.body: Open the target Asana project and locate the Add Tasks via Email option to reveal its unique, secure destination address.

steps.heading: Copy the address and draft your email
steps.body: Copy the project email address into your Gmail or Outlook client and draft a new message just as you would to any contact.

steps.heading: Format the subject and body
steps.body: Write your subject line as the task title, since Asana converts it automatically, and use the email body for the task description.

steps.heading: Use CC and syntax to assign and set dates
steps.body: CC the assignee's Asana-linked email and use the platform's recognized syntax to auto-set due dates directly from your email draft.

steps.heading: Send and verify the task
steps.body: Send the email, then refresh your Asana dashboard to confirm the new task appeared with the correct title, description, and attachments.

faq.question: Where do I find the project's unique email address?
faq.answer: Open the project menu inside Asana and look for the Add Tasks via Email option, which reveals the project-specific address to copy.

faq.question: Can I attach files by forwarding an email?
faq.answer: Yes, any attachments included in the forwarded or drafted email carry over and attach to the newly created task.

faq.question: Does this work from any email provider?
faq.answer: Yes, it works from any email client, including Gmail and Outlook, since it simply relies on sending to the project's address.

faq.question: Why didn't my task pick up the assignee I CC'd?
faq.answer: The CC'd address must match an email tied to an existing Asana account with access to that project, otherwise the assignment won't apply.
